lines.text: Larkspur? My father told me to listen for you.
But that station is empty. It burns up in sixty days.
Her name was Inés. Inés Hale.
The company had told the world that Larkspur was empty. On day three sixty, they would bring it down. Into the ocean.
With us on it.
Two people, sixty days, and a company that wanted us gone.
Day three hundred. Envelope ten. Keep talking to her. Every pass.
So we did. Every pass, ten minutes. Inés recorded everything.
She was eighteen. She stayed up every night at her radio, waiting for us to fly over.
She posted the recordings.
People said they were fake.
Then an amateur astronomer photographed the station. Its lights were on.
Empty stations don't turn their lights on.
And then Hale went public.
He told them everything. The fake leak. The gauges. The two of us.
Day three hundred thirty. Envelope eleven.
Two seats on the next ship. I made sure.
Two seats. Not one.
He had planned it from day one.
Water: ten percent.
Day three fifty-nine. Inés, on the last pass: a rescue is launching. Five days.
For the first time in a year, I let myself think about home.
Mara said she wanted to see rain.
Day three sixty.
The station shook.
The engines fired. On their own.
The deorbit burn.
We were coming *down.*
